# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 67 (Bi-Vb Pc67)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc67
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 67
**Title (English, from literature):** Ordaining a trained married girl without approval
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 67, titled *Paripuṇṇadvādasavassa-sikkhita-gihigata-asammata* ("Ordaining a trained married girl without approval"), belongs to the Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a nun commits a pācittiya offense if she ordains a married woman (*gihigatā*) who has reached the age of twelve and completed the two-year training in the six rules (*chasu dhammesu sikkhitasikkhā*), but has not received formal authorization or agreement (*vuṭṭhānasammuti* / *asaṃmatā*) from the Order [Hüsken 1997]. As discussed by Ute Hüsken, this rule has no counterpart among the bhikkhus' training rules; it presupposes that a girl married by age ten could undergo the required two-year probationary period and qualify for ordination at age twelve, provided the formal consent of the community has been granted [Hüsken 1997]. Modern translations of the rule include an English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
